text:
acme_poc: Hey team — during a demo this morning our org credits dropped to 0 mid-run and the API kept returning 429, but the billing UI still shows the monthly refill scheduled in ~6 hours. Can someone explain why they were exhausted early?

sarah_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error payload you saw and the timestamp of the request?

acme_poc: Here's the curl we used and the response snippet: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}'``` Response: ```{\n  \"error\": \"rate_limited\",\n  \"code\": 429,\n  \"message\": \"Monthly credits exhausted\",\n  \"x-credits-remaining\": 0\n}``` Happened around 2026-03-10T09:08:12Z. We were only ~85% through the month.

mike_eng: Thanks — can you also confirm org id and whether you had any large batch jobs or import jobs running ~09:00-09:10?

acme_poc: Org ID ACME-42. No batch jobs scheduled; just the demo traffic (three parallel sessions). We did have a CI test that retried a failing upload around 08:59 but nothing huge.

sam_infra: tagging monitor-bot to pull infra metrics for that org and the billing cutover logs. @monitor-bot any anomalies?

monitor-bot: Alert: unusual token draw spike detected for org ACME-42 between 09:05:00Z and 09:09:30Z — 1.8M tokens consumed in 4.5m. Source IPs: 3 distinct. Top route: /v1/generate.

oliver_billing: Looking at the billing ledger — there was a scheduled plan migration for ACME-42 at 2026-03-10T09:00:00Z (internal migration job to migrate promo credits). It completed at 09:02:12Z. Migration included a quota recompute which temporarily set available tokens to 0 until balance reconciliation finished (~09:08). That could explain the visible 0 and the 429s.

acme_poc: So migration put us to 0? But UI still showed upcoming refill later. Why didn't the recompute restore available credits faster?

mike_eng: Two separate systems: the rate-limit enforcement checks the canonical ledger; the UI reads a cached display value. During the migration we observed a brief ledger lock that held back the reconciliation write. UI cache TTL meant the front-end still showed the old balance until it refreshed. Enforcement saw 0 and returned 429.

sam_infra: We also saw a replay of several in-flight retries from a third-party integration that retried on 500s and caused a token spike right after the migration window. That amplified the depletion.

acme_poc: Ugh — that combination explains it. Is there anything you can do to refund or unblock? Our demo was impacted.

sarah_support: We can credit back the demo run tokens as a one-off and adjust your org so the UI and ledger are consistent. To proceed we need the request IDs for a few failed calls (if available) or the exact time window (we have 09:05–09:09 from monitor-bot).

acme_poc: I have a couple of request IDs from client logs: r-93a1, r-93a2, r-93a7. Thanks.

oliver_billing: I submitted a manual ledger adjustment + temporary grace allowance for ACME-42 to cover the 1.8M token spike. Also filed invoice note referencing migration job #MG-772. You should see the credits restored within 5 minutes; enforcement was updated so queued requests after 09:10 should succeed.

mike_eng: Action items: 1) ops will add a short window where migration jobs hold a soft-lock but allow existing in-flight requests to finish (low risk) — PR in staging. 2) alerting: create a composite alert for: migration-complete AND ledger-lock-duration > 10s. 3) UI cache TTL will be tightened for accounts undergoing ledger operations.

sam_infra: Rolling the soft-lock change now to staging, will monitor.

acme_poc: Credits just flipped back, API calls are succeeding again. Thank you all for the fast turnaround. :heart:

sarah_support: Glad it's fixed — we've added credits to cover the demo and added a postmortem note. We'll follow up with the migration/locking mitigations timeline. Leaving this thread open until mitigations are in prod. :thumbsup:

acme_poc: Appreciate it. Keeping thread open for the follow-up.

mike_eng: Leaving notes: root cause = ledger recompute during promo-plan migration + concurrent retry storm. Mitigations tracked in GH issue #INF-1289.

sarah_support: Closing loop once INF-1289 is merged and deployed to prod. Thanks everyone.
